transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi. Thank you for seeing me. I, um, I guess I'm here because things have just gotten really overwhelming lately, and I don't entirely know why I can't just handle it like a normal person. You see, for the longest time, I was just doing my art for fun, you know? Just making things, enjoying the process, not really worrying about anything else. But everyone kept telling me, "Oh, you should sell this, you should make a business out of it," and so a few months ago, I finally decided to try turning it into a real freelance thing. I thought it would be great, getting to do what I love all day. But ever since I made it official, it's just been... it's been a lot. 

I keep getting so wound up over the business side of things. Like, invoices and client messages—especially the client messages. Every time my phone buzzes with an email, my chest gets all tight, and I just start thinking about all the things I have to do and how I might mess it up or say the wrong thing. So instead of just dealing with it, I avoid them. I tell myself I'll look at it later, but then later comes and I still can't do it. And it just builds and builds until I'm literally sitting at my kitchen table, just crying over an email I haven't even opened yet. And because my head is so wrapped up in all this stress about the freelance stuff, I'm starting to drop the ball on normal, everyday things. Like, the other day I completely forgot to pay my electric bill, which is so unlike me, but I was just so panicked about a commission I was working on that it completely slipped my mind. It's just... it's becoming a real problem, and I don't know how to stop spiraling over it.
You mentioned avoiding client messages; do you avoid other things besides emails and invoices as well?

Um, no, I don't think so. Not really. I mean, I've been trying to think if there's anything else, but it really just seems localized to the business side of things. Like, I still go to the grocery store just fine. I actually went yesterday because I needed to pick up some of that specific chamomile and lavender tea I like—I read somewhere that it's supposed to help with stress, so I thought maybe if I make a cup before I open my laptop, it would help calm my nerves, though it hasn't really worked yet. But anyway, I don't avoid the store, or running errands, or anything like that. 

If my mom calls, or if my friends text me in our group chat to see if I want to grab a coffee, I reply right away. I don't get that awful tight feeling in my chest with them at all. I can talk to them for hours. And I still do my chores around the apartment, mostly. Well, except for forgetting that electric bill I mentioned, but that was genuinely just me forgetting because my brain was so full of panic, not me actively avoiding paying it, you know? I still take my dog out every morning right on schedule, too. 

It's literally just... just the freelance stuff. If I'm just painting or sketching for myself, I don't avoid my desk at all. I still love doing that. But the absolute second it involves a spreadsheet, or an invoice, or a client asking for an update on a commission piece, that's when I completely freeze up and just have to walk away and do literally anything else. So, yeah, I'm pretty sure it's just the business things. I haven't noticed myself hiding from anything else in my life.
Do you ever feel anxious when interacting with people in social situations, outside of your freelance work?

No, not really. I mean, I've always been a little bit on the quieter side, I guess, but I wouldn't say I get anxious around people. Like, I don't get that awful chest-tightening feeling when I'm just hanging out with my friends or talking to the cashier at the grocery store. Actually, I really enjoy seeing my friends. We have this little tradition where we get together every other Sunday for brunch at this diner downtown—it's this really cute, retro place that has the best blueberry pancakes, and we just sit there for hours drinking coffee and catching up. I never feel nervous about going to that. Or even just running into a neighbor in the hallway of my building, you know? I'll stop and chat about the weather or ask how their cat is doing, and it's totally fine. 

It's so weird because it's like my brain has just completely compartmentalized the stress. Socializing is totally fine, safe, normal. But the second someone is a "client" instead of a "friend," even if they're being perfectly nice, it's like a switch flips and suddenly I'm terrified of saying the wrong thing or coming across as unprofessional. But yeah, outside of the freelance stuff, I'm totally fine around people. I don't overthink what I'm going to say at brunch, and I don't avoid making plans. It's really just the business interactions that send me into a panic.
Do you often have physical symptoms like headaches or stomachaches when you're feeling overwhelmed by your freelance work?

Um, physical symptoms? Like headaches or stomachaches? No, I don't really think so. I mean, I definitely get that tight feeling in my chest that I mentioned earlier, where it feels like I can't quite take a full breath, and maybe my heart beats a little faster when I see an email notification pop up on my screen. But as far as actual pain, like a headache or an upset stomach, no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. 

I actually used to get tension headaches a lot when I was in college, back when I was finishing up my associate's degree. I'd be hunched over my desk for hours studying for exams, and my neck and shoulders would get so incredibly stiff, and then this awful, dull ache would just creep up the back of my head. I used to have to take ibuprofen and lie down in a dark room with a cold washcloth over my eyes just to get it to go away. But I haven't really had those in years, thankfully. I try to be pretty good about my posture now when I'm working on my art, making sure I take breaks to stretch and roll my shoulders out. 

And my stomach is usually totally fine, too. I mean, maybe a little bit of that fluttery, nervous feeling right in the pit of my stomach when I'm really panicking about a deadline, but not an actual stomachache or anything that makes me feel sick. I'm pretty careful about what I eat, anyway. I cook most of my meals at home, lots of fresh vegetables and lean proteins, and I try not to eat too much heavy, greasy food because it just makes me feel sluggish. Like, last night I made this really amazing roasted butternut squash risotto with a little bit of sage and parmesan, and it was so comforting and delicious. So yeah, my digestion is usually pretty solid. It's really just the chest tightness and the crying and the absolute mental block when it comes to dealing with the business side of things. But no headaches or stomachaches, thankfully. I feel like that would just make everything so much worse if I felt physically ill on top of being so stressed out all the time.
Do you feel anxious when you're alone with your thoughts about your freelance work?

Um, alone with my thoughts? Yeah. Yes, absolutely. I mean, it's almost worse when I'm alone with my thoughts, honestly. Because when I'm actively trying to do the work, at least I'm... well, I'm failing at doing the work, but I'm looking at the screen, right? But when I'm just sitting by myself, especially at night, that's when my brain really just starts spinning out of control. 

Like, I'll be lying in bed, and I've got my nice, heavy duvet pulled up, and the room is perfectly dark—I even have those blackout curtains because the streetlamp outside my window used to drive me crazy—and I'll just be lying there, trying to sleep, and suddenly it's like a movie reel starts playing in my head of every single client email I haven't answered. And then I start thinking about the invoices. And then I start thinking, "What if they tell everyone I'm a flake? What if I ruin my reputation? What if I never get another commission again?" It just spirals. I'll lie there for hours, literally hours, just staring at the ceiling, feeling that horrible tightness in my chest. 

Sometimes I try to distract myself. I'll put on a podcast—usually something really boring, like a history podcast about the Roman Empire or something, just to give my brain something else to latch onto. But even then, the thoughts just kind of creep in around the edges of the audio. Or I'll try to read, but I end up reading the same paragraph over and over because I'm just thinking about that one spreadsheet I couldn't bring myself to look at earlier. It's exhausting. It's like I can't escape it, even when I'm technically "off the clock" and supposed to be relaxing. The anxiety is just always there, humming in the background, waiting for a quiet moment to just... pounce on me. So yeah, being alone with my thoughts about it is really, really hard right now.
Do you think your anxiety about freelance work is because you're afraid of failing at it?

Um, afraid of failing? I'm... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't know if "failing" is the right word, or at least, I haven't really thought about it in those exact terms before. 

Because, like, with my art itself, I know I'm good at it. I spent years practicing, especially after I finished my associate's degree, really honing my digital painting techniques. I have this whole setup in the corner of my living room with this huge drawing tablet and a special ergonomic chair—which I absolutely had to get because I can sit there for six or seven hours straight just getting the lighting and the shading right on a character's face. I love that part. So I'm definitely not afraid that my art is bad, or that I'll fail at the actual creative part of the job. People seem to genuinely like what I draw.

But the business part... I don't know if it's a fear of failing at it so much as it's just... I feel completely out of my depth? Like, when someone sends me an email asking about my rates, or they attach a contract that has all this complicated jargon about "rights in perpetuity" or commercial usage licenses, my brain just completely shuts down. I guess you could look at that and say I'm afraid of failing to be a good businessperson, but it feels more like I just don't speak the language. 

Or maybe you're right and it *is* a fear of failure? Like, maybe deep down I'm terrified that if I mess up an invoice or take too long to reply, they'll think I'm a total fraud who doesn't know what she's doing. But then again, I've made mistakes before and it was fine. I remember a couple of years ago, I had this really lovely client who wanted a memorial portrait of her golden retriever, Buster. He was such a sweet-looking dog. Anyway, I accidentally charged her for one less hour than I actually worked, and I was so embarrassed when I realized, but she was incredibly nice about it. She pointed it out, paid the difference, and even tipped me extra! So I know from experience that people can be forgiving and that a little mistake isn't the end of the world. 

So yeah, I really don't know if it's a fear of failure that's causing all this panic right now. I just can't quite put my finger on the exact "why" of it all. It just feels like this giant, insurmountable wall that I can't climb over, and I don't really know why it's suddenly so impossible for me to just do the basic administrative stuff I used to be able to handle.
Do you worry about things other than your freelance work when you're lying in bed at night?

Um, other things? Like... my personal life, or family, or things like that? No, not really. Honestly, if you took the freelance business stuff out of the equation, my life is actually really calm right now. I mean, I have a really cozy apartment, and my landlord just renewed my lease without raising the rent, which is practically a miracle these days, so I don't have to worry about moving or anything stressful like that. 

And my family is doing well, too. My mom actually just retired a few months ago, and she's been taking all these community center classes on urban gardening. Whenever we talk on the phone, she just goes on and on about her heirloom tomato plants and how she's trying to figure out how to keep the neighborhood squirrels away from them, which is honestly just really nice and normal to listen to. I don't have to worry about her at all. 

And I have a cat, Barnaby. He's this huge, fluffy orange tabby I adopted a few years ago, and he is just the most relaxed creature on the planet. He sleeps right at the foot of my bed every single night. Sometimes he even rests his little chin on my ankle. You'd think having this warm, purring cat right there would just instantly put me to sleep, right? Because it's so peaceful. But no, I'll be lying there, listening to Barnaby purr, knowing my mom is happy, knowing my rent is paid, and my brain just completely ignores all of that good stuff. 

It just zeroes right back in on the freelance work. It's like a magnet. I'll try to force myself to think about something else, like, I'll try to plan out what I'm going to buy at the grocery store the next day—you know, making a mental list of like, oat milk, spinach, maybe some of those nice honeycrisp apples if they're on sale—but before I even get to the produce section in my head, I'm suddenly panicking about whether I remembered to attach a high-resolution file to a client's Dropbox folder. 

So, yeah, it really is just the work. Everything else in my life is totally fine, which almost makes it more frustrating, you know? Because I feel like I *should* be able to just relax and enjoy my life, but I just can't turn off that one specific part of my brain. It just always circles back to the emails and the invoices.
Do you feel anxious about your freelance work all the time, or are there specific times of the day when it bothers you the most?

Um, is it all the time? I guess... well, it's kind of a mix. Like I mentioned before, night time is definitely when it gets really loud, because I'm just lying there in the dark with nothing else to focus on. But during the day... it's weird. It's not really tied to a specific hour on the clock, you know? 

Like, let me walk you through yesterday, just as an example. I woke up around 8:30, which is pretty standard for me because Barnaby—my cat—usually starts pawing at the bedroom door for his breakfast right around then. So I get up, I give him his food—it's this salmon pate stuff that honestly smells terrible first thing in the morning, but he goes absolutely crazy for it—and then I go make my coffee. I use a French press, so you have to let it steep for exactly four minutes to get it right. And during those four minutes, I'm usually totally fine. I'm just standing in my kitchen in my pajamas, looking out the window, maybe watching the neighbors across the street walk their dogs or just checking to see if it's going to rain. It's peaceful. I feel completely normal.

But then, the second I take my coffee mug and walk over to my desk in the living room... it's like a switch flips. Even if I haven't touched the mouse or opened my email yet, just looking at the blank monitor makes my stomach do this horrible little drop. So mornings can be really tough right off the bat just from the anticipation of it. 

But then, maybe around one o'clock, I'll take a break to eat a turkey sandwich and I'll put on a YouTube video—lately I've been watching these really elaborate baking tutorials where people make cakes that look like everyday objects, it's fascinating, honestly—and for twenty minutes, I completely forget about my freelance stuff. I'm just amazed by someone making a vanilla sponge cake look exactly like a running shoe. 

But the moment the video ends, or if my phone screen lights up out of the corner of my eye with literally any notification, even if it's just a weather alert, that heavy dread just comes rushing right back in. So I don't know if I'd say there's a specific time of day when it bothers me the *most*, other than bedtime. It's more like... it's always there, like a low-level hum. Like when your refrigerator is running in the background and you don't really notice it while you're talking or doing things, but the absolute second the room gets quiet, it's suddenly the only thing you can hear. So yeah, I wouldn't say it's scheduled, it just ebbs and flows depending on how distracted I manage to keep myself.
Do you feel overwhelmed or anxious when thinking about other areas of your life besides your freelance work?

Um, no, like I was saying earlier, it really isn't the other areas of my life that make me anxious on their own. It's just... well, this is actually exactly why I came in to see you in the first place. Because ever since I tried to take my art and turn it into a real freelance business, this one specific thing has just completely taken over, and it's starting to mess up the rest of my life. 

I just keep getting so incredibly wound up over things like invoices and client messages. Like, I'll see an email notification pop up from someone asking for a quote, or asking for a revision on a drawing, and instead of just clicking on it and reading it, I avoid it. I'll tell myself, "Oh, I'll just read it after I feed Barnaby," or "I'll look at it after I wash these coffee mugs," and I just keep pushing it off and pushing it off. And the longer I avoid it, the bigger and scarier it feels in my head, until the stress builds up so much that I end up just sitting there crying at my kitchen table over an email I haven't even opened yet. 

And the worst part is, because I'm spending all this mental energy avoiding the work stuff and agonizing over it, that's when I start dropping the ball on my actual life. Like, I'm not anxious *about* my bills, but because I was so paralyzed over this one freelance message last week, I completely forgot to pay my electric bill. Which is so frustrating, because I usually have this little accordion folder where I keep all my mail sorted by due date—it's even color-coded—but I was just so overwhelmed by the art business stuff that paying a simple bill just completely slipped my mind. I didn't even realize it until I got a notice in the mail with this big red "past due" stamp on it. 

So, yeah, the other areas of my life are perfectly fine, but the freelance stress is just sort of... spilling over. It's making me avoid my actual work, and then making me forget how to do totally normal stuff on top of it.
Do you think you would feel this level of anxiety if you were doing something else for work, or is it specifically related to the freelance business?

Um, honestly? I really think it is just specifically this freelance business. Because, you know, like I was just saying a second ago about why I finally decided to come in and see you... this whole thing, the crying at the kitchen table, the getting so completely wound up over a simple client message or an invoice that I just avoid it entirely... none of that ever happened before I tried to turn my art into an actual, real business. It really didn't. 

Like, if I were just doing something else for work—say, if I went back to working at that little independent bookstore I used to work at after I got my associate's degree, where you just clock in, shelve some paperbacks, maybe recommend a mystery novel to someone, and then clock out—I wouldn't be feeling like this at all. I wouldn't be bringing the stress home, and I definitely wouldn't be so paralyzed by it that I'm forgetting to do normal, everyday adult things like paying my electric bill. 

But because it's *my* art, you know? It feels so personal. And suddenly I have to be the artist and the accountant and the customer service rep all at once. So every time an invoice needs to be sent, or a client messages me about a commission, it just feels so heavy. And that's exactly when I start doing that thing I just told you about, where I just push it away and push it away until I'm a sobbing mess over my coffee mug and completely forgetting how to function in the rest of my life. 

So, yeah, I really don't think a regular job would do this to me. It's the pressure of the freelance art thing, specifically, that's making me react this way. If I were just clocking into a normal job, I'd just do the work and go home to Barnaby and that would be that. But this... this just gets under my skin in a completely different way.
Are you finding it difficult to enjoy or participate in activities you normally like because of your anxiety about freelance work?

Um, no, actually, not really. Honestly, I think it might be the exact opposite? Like, I might be enjoying my regular activities *too* much right now, if that makes sense, because I'm basically using them to hide from all the freelance stuff. 

Like, I still absolutely love reading. Since I used to work at that bookstore I mentioned, I always have this massive pile of books on my nightstand. It's completely ridiculous, it looks like a leaning tower of paperbacks that's going to collapse at any minute. And lately, instead of sitting down at my computer to draft an invoice or reply to a client, I'll tell myself, "Oh, I'll just read one quick chapter of this new mystery novel before I start working." I'm reading this cozy mystery right now that's set in a little bakery in Vermont—it's very light and fun, not heavy literature by any means, but it's exactly what I need. 

So I'll sit on the couch with Barnaby—and he loves it when I read because he just curls up right on my lap and purrs like a little motorboat—and I'll get so completely absorbed in the story that I end up reading fifty pages instead of ten. And during that whole time, I'm genuinely having a great time. I'm totally invested in figuring out who poisoned the town mayor or whatever the plot is. I don't feel numb to it, and I don't find it hard to focus on the fun parts. The enjoyment is definitely still there 100 percent. 

It's just that... well, the second I put the bookmark in and put the book down, and I remember *why* I was reading in the middle of a Tuesday afternoon instead of working on a client sketch, that's when all the guilt and the chest-tightening anxiety comes rushing back. But the actual activities themselves? No, I still really love doing them. Whether it's reading, or watching those crazy cake videos I told you about earlier, or just running the laser pointer around the living room for Barnaby... I still get a lot of joy out of all of that. If anything, they're kind of my only escape hatch right now, so I cling to them pretty hard.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since you started feeling overwhelmed by your freelance work?

Um, as for my friends and family... I mean, I guess I haven't been seeing them quite as much lately, but honestly, they aren't really the problem. It's more that I'm just so... consumed by everything else going wrong that I don't even have the brain space for socializing right now. Because, like I was telling you earlier, this whole situation is just completely affecting my freelance work and my normal home responsibilities, and it's all just piling up into this massive mountain that I can't seem to climb. 

Like, the main reason everything is so chaotic right now—and exactly why I missed that utility payment I was telling you about, and why I'm currently putting off a reply to a really nice client who just wants a simple update on a sketch—is because I've also been trying to keep up with this art display. It's this local showcase thing, they're letting me hang some of my pieces up at this really cute cafe downtown, the one with the exposed brick walls and the little string lights in the windows? Which is an amazing opportunity, it really is, and I know I should be absolutely thrilled about it. But instead, trying to keep up with getting all the pieces framed and properly wired and ready for the display, while also trying to manage the business emails... it's just... it's too much. 

So I end up doing none of it. I'll stare at the paintings I need to prep for the display, and then I'll think about the client reply I'm putting off, and then I realize I haven't sorted my color-coded mail folder, which is how the electric bill slipped through the cracks in the first place... and it's just this endless, exhausting cycle. 

So, yeah, I mean, my mom called me on Sunday and I think I talked her ear off for an hour about how stressed I am, and maybe my friends think I'm being a little flaky right now, but the relationships themselves are mostly fine. It's really just my day-to-day functioning. The home stuff and the work stuff are just completely falling apart on me while I try to juggle this display and the business side of things, and I just can't seem to get a grip on any of it.
Do you think you would feel anxious in a different work situation or is it something specific about your freelance business that causes you anxiety?

Um, yeah, I mean, like I was saying just a little bit ago, I really, truly believe it's just the freelance business that's doing this to me. Honestly, that whole cycle is the exact reason I finally made the appointment to come in here today. Because ever since I tried to take my art—which, you know, used to just be this wonderful, relaxing thing for me—and turn it into a real, actual freelance business... everything just kind of short-circuited. 

If I were doing a different job, like the bookstore I mentioned, I really don't think I'd be having these issues. But with this, I just keep getting so incredibly wound up over the business side of it. Like, an invoice needs to go out, or a client sends me a totally normal message asking about a color choice or a sketch update, and my brain just completely panics. And then my response is to just avoid them. I will literally avoid opening my email for days. I just shove it all in a mental box and pretend it doesn't exist until the pressure gets so bad that I'm literally sitting there, just crying at my kitchen table, feeling completely paralyzed by it all. 

And it takes up so much of my mental energy just trying to hide from the work emails and the invoices that I end up forgetting to do normal, basic everyday stuff... like paying that utility bill I told you about earlier. So, yeah, to answer your question again, it's definitely the freelance art business specifically that's triggering all of this, because before I tried to make it a career, I was never avoiding things until I was in tears over my coffee mug, you know? It's just this specific situation that I can't seem to handle.
Do you think you would feel anxious about other types of work or is it just the freelance business that causes you anxiety?

Um, wait, didn't you just... I mean, yeah, like I was just saying a second ago, I'm pretty positive it's just the freelance business. I really don't think other types of work would make me feel like this at all. 

Because, you know, if I went back to a normal job—like the bookstore I keep bringing up—it's just a completely different world. When I worked there, my manager, Susan—she was this really sweet lady who always wore these amazing, brightly colored chunky knit cardigans—she would just give me my tasks for the day. She'd say, "Okay, I need you to shelve the new fiction releases, organize the front display, and cover the register for an hour." And I would just do it. It was so straightforward. There was absolutely no agonizing over how much to charge someone, or worrying if my art style was exactly what they wanted, or having to draft this perfectly professional email to a client who wants to change the color of a cat's collar in a custom portrait. At the bookstore, you just scan the barcode, put the book in a bag, smile, and say have a great day. 

And the best part about other types of work is that when your shift is over, you just leave. You walk out the door, you go home, and you don't think about it again until your next shift. But with this freelance stuff, it's... it's just *always* there. It's in my living room, it's on my phone, it's sitting in my inbox staring at me while I'm trying to eat breakfast. There's no manager telling me what to do, which means I have to be the manager, and I am clearly a terrible manager because my main coping mechanism is to just avoid everything until I'm a crying mess at the kitchen table. 

So, yeah, just to reiterate what I was saying before... I really think if I were doing literally anything else where someone else was in charge of the business side of things, I'd be completely fine. It's specifically the pressure of running the freelance business myself that's making me completely freeze up.
Do you think you would feel anxious if you had to manage the business side of things in a different type of freelance work, not just your art?

Oh, wow, um... I actually... I don't really know? I've honestly never even thought about that before. 

Because, you see, art has just always been my one main thing. Ever since I took those design and studio classes when I was getting my associate's degree, my entire focus has just been on the creative process itself. So the idea of doing a totally different kind of freelance work—like, I don't know, freelance writing, or being a virtual assistant, or maybe freelance graphic design for corporate logos where it's very rigid and not really expressive... I honestly couldn't tell you how I'd react to managing the business side of that. 

Part of me thinks that maybe the business stuff itself is just universally terrifying to me. Like, keeping track of the expenses and the invoices—I actually have this old Nike shoebox in my closet right now that is just absolutely overflowing with receipts that I was supposed to organize in a spreadsheet three months ago, and just looking at the box makes my chest tight. So maybe the whole self-employment, tax-form, managing-your-own-schedule thing would make me anxious no matter what the actual service was that I was providing. 

But then... then another part of me thinks, well, maybe it's so much worse right now specifically because it's my *art*, you know? Because art is just so deeply personal. When I send out a custom piece, I'm putting a piece of myself out there. So if a client is unhappy, or if I have to negotiate a price, it feels incredibly vulnerable. It feels like they are evaluating *me*. Whereas if I were doing something totally objective—like freelance bookkeeping, where it's just numbers on a page and there's no personal feelings involved—maybe drafting an email to a client wouldn't feel so paralyzing? Maybe I wouldn't be avoiding my inbox if the emails were just about spreadsheets instead of my paintings?

But really, I just... I have absolutely no idea. I've never tried any other kind of freelance work in my life, so it's incredibly hard to say if it's the "freelance" part or the "art" part that's the main culprit for why I'm struggling so much. I really don't have an answer for that. All I know for sure is that the combination of the two right now is just completely doing me in.
Do you think you would feel less anxious about your freelance work if someone else handled the business and management tasks for you?

Oh, my gosh, yes. Like, absolutely, one hundred percent yes. If I had an agent or, like, a business manager or someone to just take all of that off my plate, I think it would change my entire life. 

Because, I mean, like I've been saying, that is exactly why I came in here to see you today. Ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I just... I keep getting so incredibly wound up over the invoices and the client messages. If someone else could just step in and say, "Hey, I'll handle sending this invoice," or "I'll reply to this client who wants a different shade of blue," I could just focus on the actual painting. I could just be the artist. 

But right now, having to be the artist *and* the manager is what's causing this whole awful cycle. I get so wound up over having to draft a professional response or figure out what to charge that my brain just shuts down, and I avoid them entirely. I will literally just close my laptop and walk away, and I avoid it and avoid it until the anxiety builds up so much that I'm just sitting there crying at my kitchen table. 

And it takes up so much space in my head, you know? Just the dread of having to deal with the business side. It’s like this heavy cloud hanging over me every single day, to the point where I'm forgetting to do totally normal stuff... like paying that utility bill I told you about. My brain is just so fried from panicking over freelance emails that I can't even remember to keep my own lights on. 

So if I just had someone else doing the management tasks, I really don't think I'd be paralyzed like this. I wouldn't be crying over my coffee, and I wouldn't be getting past-due notices in the mail. I would just be painting! So, yeah, I really, truly think if I had someone else handling the business side, I would be completely fine. It's just... I don't have anyone else, so it's all on me, and I'm just completely falling apart trying to juggle it all.
Do you think your anxiety about freelance work is causing you to avoid tasks related to it?

Oh, definitely. I mean, yeah, like I was just saying a second ago, that is exactly why I finally made the appointment to come in here. Because ever since I tried to take my art—which used to just be this really peaceful, relaxing thing for me—and turn it into a real freelance business, I just... I keep getting so completely wound up over these invoices and client messages. 

It's like, I'll sit down at my desk with my coffee, feeling okay, and then I open my email and see a message asking for a price quote or a revision, and my stomach just completely drops. So instead of just dealing with it right then and there like a normal, functional adult would, I just avoid them. I will physically close my laptop and walk away.
